======================================================================
ARTICLE: Mobile operating system
WIKIPEDIA REVISION TEXT
======================================================================

{{Short description|Operating system that operates a mobile device}}
{{for|a list|Comparison of mobile operating systems}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2023}}

A '''mobile operating system''' is an [[operating system]] used for [[smartphone]]s, [[tablet computer|tablet]]s, [[smartwatch]]es, [[smartglasses]], or other non-laptop [[personal computing|personal]] [[mobile computing device]]s. While computers such as [[laptop]]s are "mobile", the operating systems used on them are usually not considered mobile, as they were originally designed for [[desktop computer]]s that historically did not have or need specific ''mobile'' features. This "fine line" distinguishing mobile and other forms has become blurred in recent years, due to the fact that newer devices have become smaller and more mobile, unlike the [[computer hardware|hardware]] of the past. Key factors blurring this line are the introduction of tablet computers, light laptops, and the hybridization of the [[2-in-1 PC]]s.

Mobile operating systems combine features of a [[desktop computer]] operating system with other features useful for mobile or handheld use, and usually including a wireless built-in modem and [[SIM card|SIM]] tray for telephone and data connection. In 2024, approximately '''1.22 billion smartphones were sold globally''', marking a 7% increase over the previous year and a solid rebound after two consecutive years of declines.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 29, 2018 |title=Canalys: Smartphone market grows 7% in 2024, Apple leads |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/smartphone_market_grows_7_in_2024_apple_leads-news-66369.php |access-date=4 February 2025 |website=GSMArena |publisher=GSMarena.com}}</ref> Sales in 2012 were 1.56 billion; sales in 2023 were 1.43 billion<ref name=":1" /> with 53.32% being [[Android (operating system)|Android]].<ref name=":2"/> Android alone has more sales than the popular desktop operating system [[Microsoft Windows]], and smartphone use (even without tablets) outnumbers desktop use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Operating System Market Share Worldwide |url=https://gs.statcounter.com/os-market-share |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=StatCounter Global Stats |language=en}}</ref>

Mobile devices, with mobile communications abilities (for example, [[smartphone]]s), contain two mobile operating systems. The main user-facing software platform is supplemented by a second low-level proprietary real-time operating system which operates the radio and other hardware. Research has shown that these low-level systems may contain a range of security vulnerabilities permitting malicious base stations to gain high levels of control over the mobile device.<ref>{{cite web |last=Holwerda |first=Thom |title=The second operating system hiding in every mobile phone |website=[[OSNews]] |date=November 12, 2013 |url=https://www.osnews.com/story/27416/the-second-operating-system-hiding-in-every-mobile-phone/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113173925/http://www.osnews.com/story/27416/The_second_operating_system_hiding_in_every_mobile_phone |archive-date=November 13, 2013}}</ref>

Mobile operating systems have had the most use of any operating system since 2017 (measured by web use).<ref name=":1">TechFoogle, June 30, 2019, [https://www.techfoogle.com/top-10-mobile-operating-system Top 10 Mobile Operating System] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190630110045/https://www.techfoogle.com/top-10-mobile-operating-system |date=June 30, 2019}}</ref>

==Timeline==
{{See also|History of tablet computers}}
{{update|section|date=January 2025}}
Mobile operating system milestones mirror the development of [[mobile phone]]s, [[personal digital assistant|PDA]]s, and smartphones:

===Pre-1990===
* 1990–2010 – [[Mobile phone]]s use [[embedded system]]s to control operation.

===1993–1999===
* 1993
** April – [[PenPoint OS]] by [[GO Corp.]] become available on the [[AT&T Corporation|AT&T]] [[EO Personal Communicator]].<ref name="PenPointOS">{{cite book |isbn=0-14-025731-4 |author=[[Jerry Kaplan]] |year=1994 |publisher=Penguin Books |location=New York |title=Startup: a Silicon Valley adventure}}</ref><ref name="PhabletHistory">{{cite web |title=Enter the Phablet: A History of Phone-Tablet Hybrids |publisher=PCmag |date=February 13, 2012 |last=Segan |first=Sasha |access-date=September 6, 2019 |url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/enter-the-phablet-a-history-of-phone-tablet-hybrids |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411120557/http://www.pcmag.com/slideshow/story/294004/enter-the-phablet-a-history-of-phone-tablet-hybrids |archive-date=April 11, 2017}}</ref>
** August – [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] launches [[Newton OS]] running on their [[Apple Newton|Newton]] series of portable computers.
* 1994
** March – [[Magic Cap]] OS by [[General Magic]] is first introduced on the [[Sony]] [[Magic Link]] [[personal digital assistant|PDA]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pencomputing.com/magic_cap/|title=Pen Computing Magazine: Magic Cap/DataRover Resource|website=www.pencomputing.com}}</ref>
** August – The first smartphone, the [[IBM Simon]], has a touchscreen, [[email]], and PDA features.<ref name="SimonTurns20">{{cite magazine |url=https://time.com/3137005/first-smartphone-ibm-simon/ |title=First Smartphone Turns 20: Fun Facts About Simon |last=Aamoth |first=Doug |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=August 18, 2014 |access-date=August 18, 2019}}</ref>
* 1996
** March – The [[Palm, Inc.|Palm]] [[Pilot 1000]] personal digital assistant is introduced with the [[Palm OS]] mobile operating system.
** August – Nokia releases the [[Nokia 9000 Communicator]] running an integrated system based on the [[PEN/GEOS 3.0]] OS from [[Geoworks]].<ref name="NokiaCommunicatorPress">{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=First GSM-based communicator product hits the market Nokia Starts Sales of the Nokia 9000 Communicator |url=http://company.nokia.com/en/news/press-releases/1996/08/15/first-gsm-based-communicator-product-hits-the-market-nokia-starts-sales-of-the-nokia-9000-communicator |website=Nokia |date=August 15, 1996 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603191142/http://company.nokia.com/en/news/press-releases/1996/08/15/first-gsm-based-communicator-product-hits-the-market-nokia-starts-sales-of-the-nokia-9000-communicator |archive-date=June 3, 2016 |url-status=dead |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref><ref name="Nokia9000Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Nokia 9000 Communicator {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=879&c=nokia_9000_communicator |website=PhoneDB |date=October 13, 2007 |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref>
* 1997 – [[EPOC (operating system)|EPOC32]] first appears on the [[Psion Series 5]] PDA. Release 6 of EPOC32 will later be renamed to [[Symbian OS]].
* 1998 – [[Symbian Ltd.]] is formed as a joint venture by [[Psion (computers)|Psion]], [[Ericsson]], [[Motorola]], and Nokia,<ref name="PsionHistory">{{cite news |url=https://stevelitchfield.com/historyofpsion.htm |title=The History of Psion |first=Steve |last=Litchfield |orig-year=1998 |year=2005 |publisher=UK Online |work=Palmtop Magazine |access-date=December 27, 2008}}</ref> Psion's [[EPOC (operating system)|EPOC32]] OS becomes Symbian's EPOC operating system,<ref name="Nokia9210Press">{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=The Nokia 9210 Communicator heralds the dawn of mobile multimedia |url=http://press.nokia.com/2000/11/21/the-nokia-9210-communicator-heralds-the-dawn-of-mobile-multimedia/ |website=Nokia |date=November 21, 2000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212112345/http://press.nokia.com/2000/11/21/the-nokia-9210-communicator-heralds-the-dawn-of-mobile-multimedia/ |archive-date=December 12, 2013 |url-status=dead |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> and is later renamed to Symbian OS. Symbian's OS was used by those companies and several other major mobile phone brands, but especially Nokia.
* 1999
** June – [[Qualcomm]]'s [[Qualcomm pdQ|pdQ]] becomes the first smartphone with [[Palm OS]].<ref name="QualcommPDQannounced">{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Qualcomm Unveils "pdQ" CDMA Digital Smartphone |url=https://www.qualcomm.com/news/releases/1998/09/21/qualcomm-unveils-pdq-cdma-digital-smartphone |date=September 21, 1998 |website=Qualcomm |language=en |access-date=June 13, 2019}}</ref><ref name="QualcommPDQreleased">{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Qualcomm's pdQ Smartphone Provides Ideal Platform For Wireless Business Solutions |url=https://www.qualcomm.com/news/releases/1999/06/15/qualcomm-s-pdq-smartphone-provides-ideal-platform-wireless-business |website=[[Qualcomm]] |date=June 15, 1999 |access-date=September 29, 2019}}</ref><ref name="pdQ800Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Qualcomm pdQ 800 {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=1150&c=qualcomm_pdq_800 |website=PhoneDB |date=February 28, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2019}}</ref><ref name="pdQ1900Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Qualcomm pdQ 1900 {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=1151&c=qualcomm_pdq_1900 |website=PhoneDB |date=February 28, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2019}}</ref>
** October – [[Series 40|Nokia S40]] Platform is officially introduced along with the [[Nokia 7110]], the first phone with [[T9 (predictive text)|T9]] [[predictive text]] input<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mobic.com/oldnews/9909/nokia_unveils_new_media_phones_f.htm |title=Nokia unveils new media phones for mobile internet access First WAP 1.1 compliant phones for Americas market |website=www.mobic.com |access-date=September 26, 2019}}</ref> and a [[Wireless Application Protocol]] (WAP) browser for accessing specially formatted Internet data.<ref name="Nokia7110unveiled">{{cite press release |title=Nokia unveils the world's first media phone for Internet access |url=http://press.nokia.com/PR/199902/777256_5.html |date=February 23, 1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010827093408/http://press.nokia.com/PR/199902/777256_5.html |archive-date=August 27, 2001 |access-date=September 26, 2019}}</ref>

===2000s===
* 2000 – The [[Ericsson R380]] is released with EPOC32 Release 5, marking the first use on a phone of what's to become known as Symbian OS (as of Release 6).<ref name="EricssonR380PDAphone">{{cite web |url=http://www.cellular.co.za/ericsson_r380.htm |title=Ericsson R380 PDA & Phone |publisher=CellularOnline |access-date=April 27, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030000/http://www.cellular.co.za/ericsson_r380.htm |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="EricssonR380Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Ericsson R380 / R380s {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=1062&c=ericsson_r380__r380s |website=PhoneDB |date=January 25, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2019}}</ref>
* 2001
** June – Nokia's Symbian [[Series 80 (software platform)|Series 80]] platform is first released on the [[Nokia 9210 Communicator]]<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Nokia 9210 Communicator Device Specs |url=http://pdadb.net/index.php?m=specs&id=886&c=nokia_9210_communicator |website=PhoneDB |date=October 16, 2007 |access-date=September 28, 2019}}</ref> This is the first phone running an OS branded as Symbian, and the first phone using that OS that allows user installation of additional software.
** September – [[Qualcomm]]'s [[Binary Runtime Environment for Wireless]] (BREW) platform on their [[REX OS|REX]] [[real-time operating system]] (RTOS) is first released on the [[Kyocera QCP-3035]].<ref name="QualcommBREW">{{cite encyclopedia |title=[[Binary Runtime Environment for Wireless]] |encyclopedia=Wikipedia |quote="Developed in 1999, as a platform for wireless applications on CDMA-based mobile phones, it debuted in September 2001 ... Originally made for the Kyocera QCP-3035 (which was the very first Brew-enabled phone)"}}</ref>
* 2002
** March
*** [[BlackBerry Limited|BlackBerry]] releases its first smartphone, running [[Java Platform, Micro Edition|Java 2 Micro Edition]] (J2ME).<ref name="BlackBerryPhone">{{cite press release |title=RIM Introduces Java-Based BlackBerry Handheld With Integrated Phone for GSM/GPRS Networks in North America |publisher=BlackBerry |date=March 4, 2002 |url=http://www.blackberry.com/news/press/2002/pr-04_03_2002-01.shtml |access-date=September 6, 2019 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071028143020/http://www.blackberry.com/news/press/2002/pr-04_03_2002-01.shtml |archive-date=October 28, 2007}}</ref>
*** [[UIQ]] is first released, at v2.0,<ref name="UIQHistory">{{cite web |title=UIQ History |url=http://www.uiq.com/uiqhistory.html |website=UIQ Technology |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070523072447/http://www.uiq.com/uiqhistory.html |archive-date=May 23, 2007 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 26, 2019}}</ref> on [[Symbian|Symbian OS]], and becomes available later in the year on the [[Sony Ericsson P800]], the successor to the Ericsson R380.<ref name="P800HandsOn">{{cite web |last=Orlowski |first=Andrew |title=Hands on with the PDA-killer Sony P800 |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2002/04/26/hands_on_with_the_pdakiller/ |website=The Register |date=April 26, 2002 |access-date=September 26, 2019 |quote=The P800 resembles its Symbian predecessor, the R380}}</ref>
** June
*** [[Microsoft]]'s first [[Windows CE]] (Pocket PC) smartphones are introduced.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.zdnet.com/products/stories/reviews/0%2C4161%2C2824082%2C00.html |title=Microsoft jumps in the all-in-one game |last1=Morris |first1=John |last2=Taylor |first2=Josh |publisher=[[ZDNet]] |date=November 12, 2001 |access-date=May 24, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011217080411/http://www.zdnet.com/products/stories/reviews/0%2C4161%2C2824082%2C00.html |archive-date=December 17, 2001}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Audiovox Thera reviewed by PC Magazine |website=PC Magazine |last1=Brown |first1=Bruce |last2=Brown |first2=Marge |date=August 1, 2002 |url=https://www.pcmag.com/archive/audiovox-pdaphone-delivers-high-speed-data-28938 |access-date=September 6, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.phonearena.com/news/Audiovox-Thera_id11 |title=Audiovox Thera |website=PhoneArena |date=August 8, 2002 |access-date=September 6, 2019}}</ref>
*** [[Nokia]]'s Symbian [[S60 (software platform)|Series 60 (S60) platform]] is released with the [[Nokia 7650]], Nokia's first phone with a camera and [[Multimedia Messaging Service]] (MMS).<ref>{{cite press release |title=Nokia's first imaging phone marks start of Multimedia Messaging era |url=http://company.nokia.com/en/news/press-releases/2001/11/19/nokias-first-imaging-phone-marks-start-of-multimedia-messaging-era |work=Nokia |date=November 19, 2001 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924133635/http://company.nokia.com/en/news/press-releases/2001/11/19/nokias-first-imaging-phone-marks-start-of-multimedia-messaging-era |archive-date=September 24, 2016 |access-date=September 26, 2019}}</ref> S60 would form the basis of the OS on most of Nokia's smartphones until 2011, when they adopted Microsoft's [[Windows Phone 7]]. S60 was also used on some phones from [[Samsung]] and others, and later by [[Sony Ericsson]] after the consolidation of some Symbian UI variants in 2008.
** October – The [[Danger Hiptop]] (T-Mobile Sidekick in U.S.) is first released by [[Danger (company)|Danger, Inc.]], running [[Danger Hiptop#Software|DangerOS]].
* 2003 – [[Motorola]] introduces first Linux-based cellphone [[Motorola A760]] base on [[MontaVista#Mobile phones|Linux MontaVista]] distribution.
* 2005
** May – Microsoft announces [[Windows Mobile 5.0]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pocketpcfaq.com/wce/versions.htm |title=Windows CE / Windows Mobile Versions |work=pocketpcfaq.com |last=De Herrera |first=Chris |access-date=September 6, 2007}}</ref>
** November – Nokia introduces [[Maemo]] OS on the first, small Internet tablet, the [[Nokia 770 Internet Tablet|N770]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.internettablettalk.com/content/view/132/2/ |title=Nokia 770 Now Available in Europe |work=Internet Tablet Talk |date=November 3, 2005 |access-date=November 5, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051124111901/http://www.internettablettalk.com/content/view/132/2/ |archive-date=November 24, 2005}}</ref> with a 4.13" screen.
* 2006
** November – [[First International Computer|FIC]] announces Linux-based [[Openmoko Linux|OpenMoko]] platform along with its first smartphone, [[Neo1973]], at the Open Source in Mobile conference in Amsterdam<ref>{{cite web | title = Openmoko mailing list | url = http://lists.openmoko.org/pipermail/community/2010-October/063653.html | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110723051724/http://lists.openmoko.org/pipermail/community/2010-October/063653.html | archive-date = 23 July 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chen |first=Jason |date=Nov 7, 2006 |title=FIC's Linux-based Smartphone |url=http://gizmodo.com/gadgets/smartphones/fics-linuxbased-smartphone-213016.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071010134707/http://gizmodo.com/gadgets/smartphones/fics-linuxbased-smartphone-213016.php |archive-date=2007-10-10 |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=[[Gizmodo]]}}</ref>.
* 2007
** January – Apple's [[iPhone]] with iOS (named "iPhone OS" for its first three releases) is introduced as a "widescreen iPod", "mobile phone", and "Internet communicator".<ref name="Macworld2007Keynote">{{cite AV media |people=Jobs, Steve |date=January 19, 2007 |url=https://www.apple.com/quicktime/qtv/mwsf07/ |title=Macworld San Francisco 2007 Keynote Address |location=San Francisco |publisher=Apple, Inc. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070123133238/http://www.apple.com/quicktime/qtv/mwsf07/ |archive-date=January 23, 2007 |df=dmy-all}}</ref>
** February – Microsoft announces [[Windows Mobile 6.0]].<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.microsoft.com/presspass/press/2007/feb07/02-11WM6SoftwarePR.mspx |title=Windows Mobile 6 press release |publisher=Microsoft |date=February 7, 2007 |access-date=February 18, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070310090007/http://www.microsoft.com/presspass/press/2007/feb07/02-11WM6SoftwarePR.mspx |archive-date=March 10, 2007}}</ref>
** May – [[Palm, Inc.|Palm]] announces the [[Palm Foleo]], a "Mobile Companion" device similar to a [[subnotebook]] computer, running a modified [[Linux]] kernel and relying on a companion [[Palm Treo]] smartphone to send and retrieve mail, as well as provide data connectivity when away from WiFi.<ref name="PalmFoleoAnnounced">{{cite web |url=http://www.treocentral.com/content/Stories/1220-1.htm |title=Palm Announces Foleo |website=treocentral.com |last1=Bohn |first1=Dieter |last2=Adolfsson |first2=Marcus |date=May 30, 2007 |access-date=September 10, 2019}}</ref> Palm canceled Foleo development on September 4, 2007, after facing public criticism.<ref name="PalmFoleoCanceled">{{Cite web |url=http://blog.palm.com/palm/2007/09/a-message-to-pa.html |title=The Official Palm Blog: A Message to Palm Customers, Partners and Developers |access-date=September 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071109201709/http://blog.palm.com/palm/2007/09/a-message-to-pa.html |archive-date=November 9, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
** June – World's very first [[IPhone 7|iPhone]] is released in the United States.
** July – [[Openmoko|OpenMoko]]'s first smartphone - Neo1973 - is released, primarily targeting developers.
** November – [[Open Handset Alliance]] (OHA) is established, led by [[Google]] with 34 members ([[HTC]], [[Sony]], [[Dell]], [[Intel]], [[Motorola Mobility|Motorola]], [[Samsung Electronics|Samsung]], [[LG Electronics|LG]], etc.)<ref name="AndroidAnnouce">{{cite web |url=https://www.openhandsetalliance.com/press_110507.html |title=Industry Leaders Announce Open Platform for Mobile Devices |date=November 5, 2007 |access-date=November 5, 2007 |publisher=Open Handset Alliance}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Delft |first=Miguel |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/05/technology/05cnd-gphone.html?ex=1352005200&en=d7a169e184415788&ei=5088&partner=rssnyt&emc=rss |title=Google Enters the Wireless World |newspaper=New York Times |date=November 5, 2007 |access-date=September 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110234644/http://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/05/technology/05cnd-gphone.html?ex=1352005200&en=d7a169e184415788&ei=5088&partner=rssnyt&emc=rss |archive-date=November 10, 2012}}</ref>
* 2008
** February – [[LiMo Foundation]] announces the first phones running the [[LiMo Platform|LiMo]] mobile Linux distribution, from [[Motorola Mobility|Motorola]], [[NEC Corporation|NEC]], [[Panasonic|Panasonic Mobile]], and [[Samsung Electronics|Samsung]],<ref name="FirstLiMoPhones1">{{cite press release |title=LiMo Foundation™ Unveils First LiMo Handsets |url=https://www.limofoundation.org/en/limo-press-releases/limo-foundation-unveils-first-limo-handsets-3.html |website=LiMo Foundation |date=February 11, 2008}}</ref><ref name="FirstLiMoPhones2">{{cite press release |title=LiMo Foundation™ Unveils First LiMo Handsets |url=https://justamp.blogspot.com/2008/02/limo-foundation-unveils-first-limo.html |website=Just Another Mobile Phone Blog |date=February 14, 2008 |access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref> released later in the year. The LiMo Foundation later became the [[Tizen Association]] and LiMo was subsumed by [[Tizen]].
** June – Nokia becomes the sole owner of [[Symbian Ltd]].<ref name="NokiaBuysOutSymbianLtd">{{cite web |url=http://www.dailytech.com/Nokia+Offers+to+Purchase+All+Symbian+Shares+for+410M/article12178.htm |title=Nokia Offers to Purchase All Symbian Shares for $410M |last=McGlaun |first=Shane |website=DailyTech |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821030054/http://www.dailytech.com/Nokia+Offers+to+Purchase+All+Symbian+Shares+for+410M/article12178.htm |archive-date=August 21, 2016 |access-date=May 22, 2016}}</ref> The [[Symbian Foundation]] was then formed to co-ordinate the future development of the Symbian platform among the corporations using it, in a manner similar to the [[Open Handset Alliance]] with Android.<ref name="SymbianFoundationFormed">{{cite press release |title=Mobile leaders to unify the Symbian software platform and set the future of mobile free |url=http://press.nokia.com/2008/06/24/mobile-leaders-to-unify-the-symbian-software-platform-and-set-the-future-of-mobile-free/ |publisher=Nokia |date=June 24, 2008 |access-date=April 9, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325025959/http://press.nokia.com/2008/06/24/mobile-leaders-to-unify-the-symbian-software-platform-and-set-the-future-of-mobile-free/ |archive-date=March 25, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Nokia remained the major contributor to Symbian's code.
** July
*** OpenMoko releases its second device - the [[Neo FreeRunner]] smartphone.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Benny |date=July 2, 2008 |title=OpenMoko Neo Freerunner Finally Available on July 4th |url=http://gizmodo.com/5021396/openmoko-neo-freerunner-finally-available-on-july-4th |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090505061030/http://gizmodo.com/5021396/openmoko-neo-freerunner-finally-available-on-july-4th |archive-date=2009-05-05 |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=[[Gizmodo]]}}</ref>
*** Apple releases [[iPhone OS 2]] with the [[iPhone 3G]], making available Apple's [[App Store (iOS)|App Store]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.apple.com/iphone/softwareupdate/iphone2.html/ |title=iPhone OS 2 |website=apple.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080912112138/http://www.apple.com/iphone/softwareupdate/iphone2.html/ |archive-date=September 12, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.macworld.com/article/1134503/iphone2update.html |title=Review: iPhone 2.0 software update |first=Dan |last=Moren |date=July 15, 2008 |work=[[Macworld]]}}</ref>
** October – OHA releases [[Android (operating system)|Android]] 1.0 (based on [[Linux kernel]]) with the [[HTC Dream]] (T-Mobile G1) as the first Android phone.<ref name="TalkAndroidG1Event">{{cite web |url=https://www.talkandroid.com/260-t-mobile-g1-details/ |title=Android G1 Release Dates, Pricing and More |publisher=TalkAndroid.com |last=Moor |first=Chris |date=September 23, 2008}}</ref>
** November – Symbian^1, the [[Symbian Foundation]]'s touch-specific S60-based platform (equivalent to [[S60 5th edition]]) is first released on Nokia's first touchscreen Symbian phone, the [[Nokia 5800 XpressMusic]],<ref name="Nokia5800Press">{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Nokia 5800 XpressMusic now shipping |url=http://press.nokia.com/2008/11/27/nokia-5800-xpressmusic-now-shipping/ |website=Nokia |date=November 27, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120708045329/http://press.nokia.com/2008/11/27/nokia-5800-xpressmusic-now-shipping/ |archive-date=July 8, 2012 |url-status=dead |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> with a resistive screen and a stylus.<ref name="Nokia5800Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Nokia 5800 / 5800d-1 XpressMusic (Nokia Tube) {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=1336&c=nokia_5800__5800d-1_xpressmusic__nokia_tube |website=PhoneDB |date=June 17, 2008 |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> Symbian^1 being derived from S60 meant that support for [[UIQ]] disappeared and no further devices using UIQ were released.<ref name="UIQBankruptcy">{{cite web |last=Hardy |first=Ed |title=UIQ Technology Files for Bankruptcy |url=http://www.brighthand.com/news/uiq-technology-files-for-bankruptcy/ |website=Brighthand |date=January 5, 2009 |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref>
* 2009
** January
*** [[Intel]] announces [[Moblin]] 2, specifically created for [[netbook]]s that run the company's [[Intel Atom|Atom]] processor.<ref name="Moblin2">{{cite magazine |last=Ganapati |first=Priya |title=Intel Pushes New Operating System For Netbooks |url=https://www.wired.com/2009/01/intel-bets-on-m/ |magazine=Wired |date=January 30, 2009 |access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref> In April 2009 Intel turned Moblin over to the [[Linux Foundation]].
*** Palm introduces [[webOS]] with the [[Palm Pre]]<ref name="PalmPreAnnounced">{{cite web |url=https://www.palminfocenter.com/news/9668/palm-announces-the-palm-pre-smartphone/ |title=Palm Announces the Palm Pre Smartphone |last=Keilhack |first=Kris |publisher=Palminfocenter.com |date=January 8, 2009 |access-date=January 8, 2009}}</ref> (released in June).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.wealthalchemist.com/Blog/2009/06/palm-pres-coming-party-june-6th/ |title=Palm Pre's coming out party: June 6th |publisher=Wealth Alchemist |date=June 5, 2009 |access-date=July 3, 2009}}</ref> The new OS is not backward-compatible with their previous Palm OS.
** February
*** [[Palm, Inc.|Palm]] announces that no further devices with Palm OS are going to be released by the company.<ref name="NoMorePalmOSDevices">{{cite web |url=http://www.treocentral.com/content/Stories/2399-1.htm |title=No More PalmOS Devices from Palm. No Patent Fight with Apple (yet) |website=treocentral.com |last=Bohn |first=Dieter |date=February 11, 2009 |access-date=September 10, 2019}}</ref> (The last was the [[Palm Centro]], released October 14, 2007.<ref name="PalmCentroHandsOn">{{cite web |url=http://www.treocentral.com/content/Stories/1361-1.htm |title=Hands-on With the Palm Centro |website=treocentral.com |last=Ducker |first=Michael |date=September 27, 2007 |access-date=September 10, 2019}}</ref>)
*** [[Microsoft]] announces [[Windows Mobile 6.5]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.engadget.com/2009/02/16/windows-mobile-6-5-walkthrough-with-engadget/ |title=Windows Mobile 6.5 walkthrough with Engadget (now with video!) |last=Ziegler |first=Chris |publisher=Engadget |date=February 16, 2009}}</ref> an "unwanted stopgap" update to Windows Mobile 6.1 intended to bridge the gap between version 6.1 and the then yet-to-be released Windows Mobile 7 (later canceled in favor of [[Windows Phone|Windows Phone 7]]).<ref name="WM65stopgap">{{cite news |url=http://www.electronista.com/articles/09/03/05/ballmer.on.win.mobile.6.5/ |title=Ballmer: Win Mobile 6.5 an unwanted stopgap |newspaper=Electronista |date=March 5, 2009 |access-date=September 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150318235554/http://www.electronista.com/articles/09/03/05/ballmer.on.win.mobile.6.5/ |archive-date=March 18, 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="BallmerWeScrewedUp">{{cite news |url=http://news.idg.no/cw/art.cfm?id=F2F7C35E-1A64-67EA-E4BC04F120F0B898 |title=Ballmer: We 'screwed up with Windows Mobile' |newspaper=[[Computerworld]] |date=September 25, 2009 |access-date=September 4, 2019 |archive-date=October 1, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091001113618/http://news.idg.no/cw/art.cfm?id=F2F7C35E-1A64-67EA-E4BC04F120F0B898 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The first devices running it appeared in late October 2009.<ref name="ZDNetWM65devices">{{cite web |url=http://blogs.zdnet.com/microsoft/?p=1908 |title=Windows Mobile: What's coming when – All about microsoft |publisher=ZDNet.com |access-date=September 4, 2019 |archive-date=March 4, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304110726/http://blogs.zdnet.com//microsoft//?p=1908 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
** May – [[Danger Hiptop#Software|DangerOS]] 5.0 becomes available, based on [[NetBSD]].<ref name="DangerNetBSD">{{cite web |url=http://www.hiptop3.com/archives/sidekick-lx-2009-blade-will-run-netbsd/ |title=Sidekick LX 2009 / Blade Will Run NetBSD |date=January 30, 2009 |work=www.hiptop3.com |access-date=February 5, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090317022256/http://www.hiptop3.com/archives/sidekick-lx-2009-blade-will-run-netbsd/ |archive-date=March 17, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fogey.com/contemplating/?p=1023|title=How NetBSD came to be shipped by Microsoft. &#124; A Dinosaur Contemplating Asteroids|date=December 14, 2018}}</ref>
** June – Apple releases [[iPhone OS 3]] with the [[iPhone 3GS]].
** November – Nokia releases the [[Nokia N900]],<ref name="NokiaN900releasedUS">{{cite web |last=Murph |first=Darren |title=Nokia's Maemo 5-equipped N900 on sale in America for $649 |url=https://www.engadget.com/2009/11/18/nokias-maemo-5-equipped-n900-on-sale-in-america-for-649/ |website=Engadget |date=November 18, 2009 |access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref> its first and only smartphone running the [[Maemo]] OS intended for "handheld computers...with voice capability", while stating that they remain focused on [[Symbian]] [[S60 (software platform)|S60]] as their smartphone OS.<ref name="NokiaN900review">{{cite web |last=Ziegler |first=Chris |title=Nokia N900 review |url=https://www.engadget.com/2010/01/19/nokia-n900-review/ |publisher=Engadget |date=January 19, 2010 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |quote=Thing is, Nokia's been absolutely emphatic with us – Maemo's intended for handheld computers (read: MIDs) with voice capability, while S60 continues to be the choice for purebred smartphones}}</ref> (Nokia had previously released three [[Mobile Internet device]]s running Maemo, without cellular network connectivity.)

===2010s===

====2010====
* February
** [[MeeGo]] is announced, a mobile Linux distribution merging Maemo from Nokia and [[Moblin]] from Intel and Linux Foundation, to be hosted by Linux Foundation.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ryan |first=Justin |title=Maemo + Moblin=MeeGo |url=https://www.linuxjournal.com/content/maemo-moblin-meego |publisher=Linux Journal |date=February 16, 2010}}</ref> MeeGo is not backward-compatible with any previous operating system.
** [[Samsung Electronics|Samsung]] introduces the [[Bada (operating system)|Bada]] OS and shows the first Bada smartphone, the [[Samsung S8500]].<ref name="SamsungS8500Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Samsung GT-S8500 Wave 8GB {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=2248&c=samsung_gt-s8500_wave_8gb |website=PhoneDB |date=February 20, 2010 |access-date=October 17, 2019}}</ref> It was later released in May 2010.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Samsung Wave, first Bada smartphone hits the market |url=http://www.bada.com/samsung-wave-first-bada-smartphone-hits-the-market/ |work=Samsung |date=May 24, 2010 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101223231522/http://www.bada.com/samsung-wave-first-bada-smartphone-hits-the-market/ |archive-date=December 23, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
* April
** Apple releases the [[iPad]] ([[iPad (1st generation)|first generation]]) with [[iPhone OS 3]].2.<ref name="iPadAvailable">{{cite press release |url=https://www.apple.com/pr/library/2010/03/05iPad-Available-in-US-on-April-3.html |title=iPad Available in US on April 3 |publisher=[[Apple Inc.|Apple]] |date=March 5, 2010 |access-date=March 5, 2010}}</ref> This is the first version of the OS to support tablet computers. For its next major version (4.0) iPhone OS will be renamed iOS.
** [[Hewlett-Packard|HP]] acquires Palm in order to use [[webOS]] in multiple new products, including smartphones, tablets, and [[printer (computing)|printers]],<ref name="HPacquiresPalm">{{cite magazine |last=Bajarin |first=Ben |title=HP Is Committed to Its 'webOS' Platform (and It Should Be). |series=TechLand |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |publisher=Time Inc. |date=June 30, 2011 |url=https://techland.time.com/2011/06/30/hp-is-committed-to-its-webos-platform-and-it-should-be/#ixzz1QshLqoCZ |access-date=November 27, 2013}}</ref> later stating their intent to use it as the universal platform for all their devices.<ref name="HPwebOS">{{cite web |url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/mobile/hp-snubs-windows-plans-to-integrate-webos-into-pcs |title=HP snubs Windows, plans to integrate webOS into PCs |publisher=Digital Trends |date=February 9, 2011 |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref>
* May – Microsoft [[Microsoft Kin|Kin]] phone line with KIN OS (based on [[Windows CE]] and a "close cousin" to [[Windows Phone]]<ref name="KinOSWinPhone">
{{cite web |url=http://www.phonescoop.com/news/item.php?n=5969 |title=Windows Phone 7 and KIN Closer Cousins Than Thought |date=May 12, 2010 |publisher=Phone Scoop |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130131104109/http://www.phonescoop.com/news/item.php?n=5969 |archive-date=January 31, 2013}}</ref>) become available.
* June – Apple releases [[iOS 4]], renamed from iPhone OS, with the [[iPhone 4]].
* July – Microsoft [[Microsoft Kin|Kin]] phones and KIN OS are discontinued.<ref name="VerizonReturnsKins">{{cite web |url=http://www.electronista.com/articles/10/07/18/verizon.decides.against.selling.out.kin.stock/ |title=Verizon returns unsold Kin phones, pulls online sales, July 18, 2010 |publisher=Electronista.com |date=July 18, 2010 |access-date=February 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130517223829/http://www.electronista.com/articles/10/07/18/verizon.decides.against.selling.out.kin.stock/ |archive-date=May 17, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="KinIsDead">{{cite web |last=Ziegler |first=Chris |url=https://www.engadget.com/2010/06/30/microsoft-kin-is-dead/ |title=Microsoft Kin is dead |publisher=Engadget.com |date=June 30, 2010 |access-date=February 4, 2013}}</ref>
* September
** Apple releases a variant of iOS powering the new [[Apple TV (device)#Second generation|2nd generation Apple TV]].<ref name="iOSAppleTV">{{cite news |title=Apple Goes 'Wild' Over New iPods |publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |first=Ki Mae |last=Heussner |date=September 1, 2010 |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Technology/apples-ipods-unveiled-ceo-steve-jobs/story?id=11534551 |access-date=September 8, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100904133427/https://abcnews.go.com/Technology/apples-ipods-unveiled-ceo-steve-jobs/story?id=11534551 |archive-date=September 4, 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref>
** [[Symbian OS|Symbian^3]] is first released on the [[Nokia N8]].<ref name="NokiaN8Shipping">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Nokia N8 is shipping (photos) – Nokia Conversations: the official Nokia blog |url=http://conversations.nokia.com/2010/09/30/nokia-n8-is-shipping-photos/ |website=Nokia |date=September 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810095748/http://conversations.nokia.com:80/2010/09/30/nokia-n8-is-shipping-photos/ |archive-date= 2014-08-10|url-status=dead |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref><ref name="NokiaN8Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Nokia N8-00 (Nokia Vasco) {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=2379&c=nokia_n8-00__nokia_vasco |website=PhoneDB |date=May 11, 2010 |access-date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> This would be Nokia's last flagship device running Symbian (though not their last Symbian phone), before switching to [[Windows Phone 7]] for future flagship phones.
** The [[Danger Hiptop]] line and [[Danger Hiptop#Software|DangerOS]] are discontinued as a result of Microsoft's acquisition of [[Danger (company)|Danger, Inc.]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.complex.com/pop-culture/a/jason-duaine-hahn/history-of-the-sidekick | title=The History of the Sidekick: The Coolest Smartphone of All Time | first=Jason Duaine | last=Hahn | work=[[Complex Networks]] | date=September 11, 2015}}</ref>
* November
** [[Nokia]] assumes full control over Symbian as the Symbian Foundation disintegrates.<ref name="NokiaReabsorbsSymbian">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-11713192 |title=Nokia reabsorbs Symbian software |work=BBC News |date=November 8, 2010}}</ref>
** Windows Phone OS is released<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.engadget.com/2010/09/26/microsoft-prepping-windows-phone-7-for-an-october-21st-launch/ |title=Microsoft prepping Windows Phone 7 for an October 21 launch? (update: US on Nov. 8?) |first=Sean |last=Hollister |work=[[Engadget]] |publisher=[[AOL]] |date=September 26, 2010 |access-date=September 29, 2010}}</ref> on Windows Phone 7 [[List of Windows Phone 7 devices|phones]] by [[HTC]], [[LG]], Samsung, and [[Dell]]. The new OS is not backward-compatible with the prior [[Windows Mobile]] OS.<ref name="Miniman">{{cite web |url=http://pocketnow.com/thought/thoughts-on-windows-phone-7-series-btw-photon-is-dead |title=Thoughts on Windows Phone 7 Series (BTW: Photon is Dead) |first=Brandon |last=Miniman |work=Pocketnow |date=February 17, 2010 |access-date=June 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029192149/http://pocketnow.com/thought/thoughts-on-windows-phone-7-series-btw-photon-is-dead |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mobiletechworld.com/2009/09/24/steve-ballmer-wishes-windows-mobile-7-had-already-launched-but-they-screwed-up/ |title=Steve Ballmer wishes Windows Mobile 7 had already launched, but they screwed up |work=MobileTechWorld |date=September 24, 2009 |access-date=July 21, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104214039/http://www.mobiletechworld.com/2009/09/24/steve-ballmer-wishes-windows-mobile-7-had-already-launched-but-they-screwed-up/ |archive-date=November 4, 2013}}</ref>

====2011====
* February
** [[Android version history#v3.x Honeycomb|Android 3.0]] (Honeycomb), the first version to officially support tablet computers, is released on the Motorola [[Motorola Xoom|Xoom]].<ref name="Android3Xoom">{{cite web |url=http://reviews.cnet.com/motorola-xoom#reviewPage1 |title=Motorola Xoom |date=February 24, 2011 |access-date=April 8, 2011 |publisher=CNET |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110410020624/http://reviews.cnet.com/motorola-xoom/#reviewPage1 |url-status=live |archive-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref>
** [[Nokia]] abandons the Symbian OS and announces that it would use Microsoft's Windows Phone 7 as its primary smartphone platform, while Symbian would be gradually wound down.<ref name="NokiaDropsSymbian">{{cite web |url=http://www.allaboutmeego.com/news/item/12584_Nokias_new_strategy_and_struct.php/ |title=Nokia's new strategy and structure, Symbian to be a "franchise platform", MeeGo still in long term plans |website=All About MeeGo |last=Litchfield |first=Steve |date=February 11, 2011 |access-date=September 10, 2019 |archive-date=September 6, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130906135631/http://www.allaboutmeego.com/news/item/12584_Nokias_new_strategy_and_struct.php |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="RIPSymbian">{{cite web |url=https://www.engadget.com/2011/02/11/rip-symbian/ |title=RIP: Symbian |website=engadget.com |last=Ricker |first=Thomas |date=February 11, 2011 |access-date=September 10, 2019}}</ref>
* April – [[BlackBerry Tablet OS]], based on [[QNX Neutrino]] is released on the [[BlackBerry Limited|BlackBerry]] [[BlackBerry PlayBook|PlayBook]].
* July
** [[Mozilla]] announces their ''Boot to Gecko'' project (later named [[Firefox OS]]) to develop an OS for handheld devices emphasizing standards-based Web technologies,<ref name="MozBoottoGecko">{{cite web |last=Paul |first=Ryan |title=Mozilla eyes mobile OS landscape with new Boot to Gecko project |url=https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2011/07/mozilla-eyes-mobile-os-landscape-with-new-boot-to-gecko-project/ |publisher=Ars Technica |date=July 25, 2011 |access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref> similar to webOS.
** webOS 3.0, the first version to support tablet computers, is released on the HP [[HP TouchPad|TouchPad]].<ref name=webOS3>{{cite web |url=http://www.webosnation.com/webos-3-0-5-now-available-touchpad |title=webOS 3.0.5 now available for TouchPad |date=January 12, 2012 |access-date=January 12, 2012}}</ref>
* August – [[Hewlett-Packard|HP]] announces that webOS device development and production lines would be halted.<ref name="HPkillswebOS">{{cite web |title=HP kills webOS, spins off PC business to focus on software |work=AppleInsider |url=http://www.appleinsider.com/articles/11/08/18/hp_to_spin_off_pc_business_to_focus_on_enterprise_software.html |date=August 11, 2011 |access-date=August 18, 2011}}</ref> The last HP webOS version, 3.0.5, is released on January 12, 2012.<ref name="webOS305">{{Cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2012/1/12/2702658/hp-touchpad-updated-to-webos-3-0-5 |title=HP TouchPad updated to webOS 3.0.5 |last=Ziegler |first=Chris |date=January 12, 2012 |website=The Verge |access-date=August 7, 2017}}</ref>
* September
** [[MeeGo]] is introduced with the limited-release [[Nokia N9]], Nokia's first and only consumer device to use the OS.<ref name="NokiaN9last">{{cite web |first1=Josh |last1=Halliday |first2=Charles |last2=Arthur |title=Nokia N9: last of the line |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2011/sep/28/nokia-n9-last-of-line |website=the Guardian |date=September 28, 2011 |access-date=April 3, 2018}}</ref> (A small number of the [[Nokia N950]], a MeeGo phone available only to developers, were released in mid-2011.<ref>{{cite web |last=Davies |first=Chris |url=https://www.slashgear.com/nokia-n950-arriving-with-meego-developers-now-23161090/ |title=Nokia N950 arriving with MeeGo developers now |website=SlashGear |date=June 23, 2011 |access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref>)
** After Nokia's abandonment of MeeGo, Intel and the Linux Foundation announce a partnership with [[Samsung]] to launch [[Tizen]], shifting their focus from MeeGo (Intel and Linux Foundation) and [[Bada (operating system)|Bada]] (Samsung) during 2011 and 2012.<ref name="IntelSamsungLaunchTizen">{{cite web |last=Paul |first=Ryan |title=MeeGo rebooted as Intel and Samsung launch new Tizen platform |url=https://arstechnica.com/free/news/2011/09/meego-rebooted-as-intel-and-samsung-launch-new-tizen-platform.ars |publisher=Ars Technica |date=September 28, 2011 |access-date=September 28, 2011}}</ref>
* October
** Apple releases [[iOS 5]] with the [[iPhone 4S]], integrating the [[Siri]] voice assistant.
** The [[Mer (software distribution)|Mer]] project is announced, based on an ultra-portable core for building products, composed of Linux, [[HTML5]], [[QML]], and [[JavaScript]], which is derived from the MeeGo codebase.
* November – [[Fire OS]], a fork of the Android operating system, is released by [[Amazon.com]] on the [[Amazon Fire tablet|Kindle Fire]] tablet.

====2012====
* May – Nokia releases the [[Nokia 808 PureView]],<ref name="808PureViewRelease">{{cite web |last=Warren |first=Tom |title=Nokia's 41-megapixel 808 PureView phone arriving in Russia and India in May |url=https://www.theverge.com/2012/5/2/2993328/nokia-808-pureview-russia-india-may-release |website=The Verge |date=May 2, 2012 |access-date=September 27, 2019}}</ref> later confirmed (in January 2013) to be the last Symbian smartphone.<ref name="TheLastSymbianPhone">{{cite web |last=Lunden |first=Ingrid |url=https://techcrunch.com/2013/01/24/nokia-confirms-the-pure-view-was-officially-the-last-symbian-phone |title=Nokia Confirms The PureView Was Officially The Last Symbian Phone |date=January 24, 2013 |work=TechCrunch |publisher=AOL |access-date=September 14, 2015}}</ref> This phone was followed by a single last Symbian software update, "Nokia Belle, Feature Pack 2", later in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hay |first=Emma |title=Symbian Carla Cancelled, Beginning Of The End For Symbian? |url=https://www.itproportal.com/2012/05/25/symbian-carla-cancelled-beginning-of-the-end-for-symbian/ |website=ITProPortal |date=May 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106221712/https://www.itproportal.com/2012/05/25/symbian-carla-cancelled-beginning-of-the-end-for-symbian/ |archive-date=November 6, 2018 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 27, 2019}}</ref>
* July
** Finnish start-up [[Jolla]], formed by former Nokia employees, announces that MeeGo's community-driven successor [[Mer (software distribution)|Mer]]<ref>{{cite tweet |user=JollaHQ |author=Jolla |number=230579553142181888 |date=August 1, 2012 |title=@kavalczuk #MeeGo is the name people know and love. #merproject is the core OS project name.}}</ref> would be the basis of their new [[Sailfish OS|Sailfish]] smartphone OS.<ref name="JollaMeeGofaithful">{{cite web |last=Fingas |first=Jon |title=Jolla promises MeeGo will live on, plans new smartphone to reward the faithful |url=https://www.engadget.com/2012/07/07/jolla-promises-meego-will-live-on-plans-new-smartphone/ |website=Engadget |date=July 7, 2012 |access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref>
** [[Mozilla]] announces that the project formerly named ''Boot to Gecko'' (which is built atop an Android Linux kernel using Android drivers and services; however it uses no Java-like code of Android) is now [[Firefox OS]] (since discontinued) and has several handset OEMs on board.
* August – Samsung announces they will not ship further phones using their Bada OS, instead focusing on [[Windows Phone 8]] and Android.<ref>{{cite web |title=No more bada and TIZEN in 2012 |url=https://www.sammobile.com/2012/08/22/no-more-bada-and-tizen-in-2012 |work=Sammobile.com |date=August 22, 2012 |access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref>
* September – Apple releases [[iOS 6]] with the [[iPhone 5]].

====2013====
* January – [[Research in Motion|BlackBerry]] releases their new operating system for smartphones, [[BlackBerry 10]], with their [[BlackBerry Q10|Q10]] and [[BlackBerry Z10|Z10]] smartphones.<ref name="BB10release">{{cite web |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/technology/technolog/blackberry-10-launches-jan-30-two-new-phones-1C6983302 |title=BlackBerry 10 launches Jan. 30 with two new phones |last=Spoonauer |first=Mark |publisher=[[NBC News]] |date=November 12, 2012 |access-date=February 12, 2013}}</ref> BlackBerry 10 is not backward-compatible with the [[BlackBerry OS]] used on their previous smartphones.
* February – [[Hewlett-Packard|HP]] sells webOS to LG.<ref name="LGacquresWebOS">{{cite press release |url=http://www8.hp.com/us/en/hp-news/press-release.html?id=1375489#.USvx7qK-q2E |title=LG Electronics Acquires webOS from HP to Enhance Smart TV |publisher=Hewlett-Packard |date=February 25, 2013 |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref><ref name="LGbuyswebOS">{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2013/2/25/4027018/lg-buys-webos-smart-tv |title=LG buys webOS from HP for use in smart TVs |last=Byford |first=Sam |publisher=[[The Verge]] |date=February 25, 2013 |access-date=September 8, 2019}}</ref>
* September – Apple releases [[iOS 7]] with the [[iPhone 5S]] and [[iPhone 5C]].
* October
** [[Canonical Ltd.|Canonical]] announces [[Ubuntu Touch]], a version of the Linux distribution expressly designed for smartphones. The OS is built on the Android Linux kernel, using Android drivers and services, but does not use any of the Java-like code of Android.<ref name="The Verge">{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2013/1/2/3827922/ubuntu-phone-os-announcement |title=Ubuntu phone OS announced, first devices shipping in early 2014 |date=January 2, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620183009/https://www.theverge.com/2013/1/2/3827922/ubuntu-phone-os-announcement |archive-date=June 20, 2017}}</ref>
** [[Google]] releases Android KitKat 4.4.
* November – [[Jolla]] releases [[Sailfish OS]] on the [[Jolla (smartphone)|Jolla smartphone]].<ref name="JollaSmartphoneSpecs">{{Cite web |title=Jolla Smartphone specs |url=https://www.phonearena.com/phones/Jolla-Smartphone_id8153 |publisher=PhoneArena |date=September 20, 2013 |access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref>

====2014====
* February
** [[Microsoft]] releases [[Windows Phone 8.1]]
** [[Nokia]] introduces their [[Nokia X platform]] OS as an Android 4.1.2 Jelly Bean fork on the [[Nokia X family]] of smartphones.<ref>{{cite web |last=Robertson |first=Adi |url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/2/24/5440498/nokia-x-android-phone-hands-on |title=This is Nokia X: Android and Windows Phone collide |publisher=The Verge |date=February 24, 2014 |access-date=March 2, 2014}}</ref> Similar to [[Amazon.com]]'s Fire OS, it replaces Google's apps and services with ones from Nokia (such as [[Here Maps|HERE Maps]], [[Nokia Xpress]] and [[MixRadio]], and [[Nokia Store|Nokia's own app store]]) and Microsoft (such as [[Skype]] and [[Microsoft Outlook|Outlook]]), with a user interface that mimics the Windows Phone UI. After the acquisition of Nokia's devices unit, Microsoft announced in July 2014 that no more Nokia X smartphones would be introduced, marking the end of the platform just a few months later.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/7/17/5911909/microsoft-kills-off-its-nokia-android-phones |title=Microsoft kills off its Nokia Android phones |publisher=The Verge |date=April 8, 2014}}</ref>
* August – The [[Samsung ZEQ 9000|Samsung SM-Z9005 Z]] is the first phone released running Tizen, with v2.2.1 of the OS.<ref name="SamsungSMZ9005Specs">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Samsung SM-Z9005 Z (Samsung Redwood) {{!}} Device Specs |url=https://phonedb.net/index.php?m=device&id=6292&c=samsung_sm-z9005_z__samsung_redwood |website=PhoneDB |date=June 2, 2014 |access-date=October 17, 2019}}</ref>
* September
** Apple releases [[iOS 8]] with the [[iPhone 6|iPhone 6 and 6 Plus]].
** [[BlackBerry Limited|BlackBerry]] releases [[BlackBerry 10]] version 10.3 with integration with the [[Amazon Appstore]]

====2015====

==Current software platforms==
{{See also|Comparison of mobile operating systems|Comparison of smartphones|List of iPhone models|List of Windows phones}}

These operating systems often run atop [[baseband processor|baseband]] or other [[real-time operating system]]s that handle hardware aspects of the phone.

===Android===
{{Main|Android (operating system)|Android version history|List of custom Android distributions}}

Android (based on the modified [[Linux kernel]]) is a mobile operating system developed by Open Handset Alliance.<ref name="OS MS 3Q10">{{cite web |url=http://www.gartner.com/it/page.jsp?id=1466313 |title=Gartner Says Mobile Phone Sales Grew 35 Percent in Third Quarter 2010; Smartphone Sales Increased 96 Percent |date=November 10, 2010 |publisher=Gartner, Inc |at=Table 2 |access-date=February 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110113073826/http://www.gartner.com/it/page.jsp?id=1466313 |archive-date=January 13, 2011}}</ref> The base system is [[free and open-source|open-source]] (and only the kernel [[copyleft]]), but the apps and drivers which provide functionality are increasingly becoming [[proprietary software|closed-source]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Amadeo |first1=Ron |title=Google's iron grip on Android: Controlling open source by any means necessary |url=https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2018/07/googles-iron-grip-on-android-controlling-open-source-by-any-means-necessary/ |website=Ars Technica |language=en-us |date=July 21, 2018}}</ref> Besides having the largest installed base worldwide on smartphones, it is also the most popular operating system for [[Turing machine|general purpose computers]]{{Explain|Some internal joke? [[Turing machine]] in its strict sense is obsolete and neither that article nor [[Computer]] contain even the word "Android" as of date.|date=July 2020}} (a category that includes desktop computers and mobile devices), even though Android is not a popular operating system for regular (desktop) [[personal computer]]s (PCs). Although the Android operating system is [[free and open-source software]],<ref name="ICS is coming to AOSP">{{cite web |url=https://groups.google.com/g/android-building/c/T4XZJCZnqF8/m/WkWhGUYb4MAJ |title=ICS is coming to AOSP |website=groups.google.com}}</ref> in devices sold, much of the software [[product bundling|bundled]] with it (including Google apps and vendor-installed software) is [[proprietary software]] and closed-source.<ref>[https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2013/09/balky-carriers-and-slow-oems-step-aside-google-is-defragging-android/ Balky carriers and slow OEMs step aside: Google is defragging Android.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130903011541/http://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2013/09/balky-carriers-and-slow-oems-step-aside-google-is-defragging-android/ |date=September 3, 2013}} [https://arstechnica.com/ Ars Technica] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703174116/https://arstechnica.com/ |date=July 3, 2017}}. Retrieved December 24, 2013.</ref>

Android's releases before [[Android Eclair|2.0]] (1.0, [[Android Cupcake|1.5]], [[Android Donut|1.6]]) were used exclusively on mobile phones. Android 2.x releases were mostly used for mobile phones but also some tablets. [[Android Honeycomb|Android 3.0]] was a tablet-oriented release and does not officially run on mobile phones. Both phone and tablet compatibility were merged with [[Android Ice Cream Sandwich|Android 4.0]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=BasuMallick |first1=Chiradeep |title=What Is Android OS? History, Features, Versions, and Benefits |url=https://www.spiceworks.com/soft-tech/android-os/ |website=Spiceworks |access-date=11 June 2026 |date=19 March 2024}}</ref>

Many OEMs ship their devices with [[List of custom Android distributions|custom skins]] and numerous forks of Android are available to use as custom ROMs.

===Wear OS===
{{Main|Wear OS}}
Wear OS (also known simply as Wear and formerly Android Wear) is a version of Google's Android operating system designed for smartwatches and other [[wearable computer|wearables]]. By pairing with mobile phones running Android version 6.0 or newer, or iOS version 10.0 or newer with limited support from Google's pairing application, Wear OS integrates [[Google Assistant]] technology and mobile notifications into a smartwatch form factor.

In May 2021 at [[Google I/O]], Google announced a major update to the platform, internally known as Wear OS 3.0. It incorporates a new visual design inspired by Android 12, and Fitbit exercise tracking features. Google also announced a partnership with Samsung Electronics, who is collaborating with Google to unify its Tizen-based smartwatch platform with Wear OS, and has committed to using Wear OS on its future smartwatch products starting with [[One UI]] Watch 3.0. The underlying codebase was also upgraded to Android 11.

===ChromeOS===
{{Main|ChromeOS}}

ChromeOS is an operating system designed by Google that is based on the Linux kernel and uses the [[Google Chrome]] web browser as its principal user interface. As a result, ChromeOS primarily supports [[web application]]s. Google announced the project in July 2009, conceiving it as an operating system in which both applications and user data reside in the [[cloud computing|cloud]]: hence ChromeOS primarily runs [[web application]]s.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chromium.org/chromium-os/chromiumos-design-docs/chromium-os-kernel |title=Kernel Design |website=The Chromium Projects}}</ref>

Due to increase of popularity with 2-in-1 PCs, most recent Chromebooks are introduced with touch screen capability, with Android applications starting to become available for the operating system in 2014. And in 2016, access to Android apps in the entire [[Google Play Store]] was introduced on supported ChromeOS devices. With the support of Android applications, there are Chromebook devices that are positioned as tablet based instead of notebooks.

ChromeOS is only available pre-installed on hardware from Google manufacturing partners. An open source equivalent, [[ChromiumOS]], can be [[compiled]] from downloaded [[source code]]. Early on, Google provided design goals for ChromeOS, but has not otherwise released a technical description.

===Sailfish OS===
{{Format|date=March 2020}}{{Main|Sailfish OS}}
Sailfish OS is an operating system made by [[Jolla]]. It is open source with [[GNU General Public License]] (GPL) for [[middleware]] stack core which comes from MER. Sailfish, due to Jolla's business model, alliances with various partners and intentional design of OS internals, is capable to adopt in several layers of third-party software, including Jolla software e.g. Jolla's UI is proprietary software (closed source), so such components can be proprietary with many kinds of licences. However, users can replace them with open source components like NEMO UI instead Jolla's UI.

After [[Nokia]] abandoned in 2011 the [[MeeGo]] project, most of the MeeGo team left Nokia, and established Jolla as a company to use MeeGo and Mer business opportunities. The MER standard allows it to be launched on any hardware with kernel compatible with MER. In 2012, Linux Sailfish OS based on MeeGo and using middleware of MER core stack distribution was launched for public use. The first device, the [[Jolla (smartphone)|Jolla smartphone]], was unveiled on May 20, 2013. In 2015, Jolla Tablet was launched and the [[BRICS]] countries declared it an officially supported OS there. Jolla started licensing Sailfish OS 2.0 for third parties. Some devices sold are updateable to Sailfish 2.0 with no limits.

[[Nemo Mobile]] is a community-driven OS, similar to Sailfish but attempting to replace its proprietary components, such as the user interface.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://wiki.merproject.org/wiki/Nemo |title=Nemo |website=Mer Wiki |access-date=August 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ohloh.net/p/nemomobile |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130729164508/http://www.ohloh.net/p/nemomobile |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 29, 2013 |title=The Nemo Mobile Open Source Project on Ohloh |publisher=Ohloh.net |access-date=August 20, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{citation |author=Marko Saukko |title=Porting Nemo Mobile and Mer Project to new Hardware |publisher=[[FOSDEM|FOSDEM 2013]] |url=https://archive.fosdem.org/2013/schedule/event/porting_nemo_mobile_and_mer/ |date=February 3, 2013 |access-date=July 29, 2013}}</ref>

===SteamOS===
{{Main|SteamOS}}
SteamOS is a [[Linux distribution]] developed by [[Valve Corporation|Valve]]. It incorporates Valve's popular namesake [[Steam (service)|Steam]] video game storefront and is the primary operating system for [[Steam Machines]] and the [[Steam Deck]]. SteamOS is [[open source]] with some closed source components.

SteamOS was originally built to support streaming of video games from one [[personal computer]] to the one running SteamOS within the same network, although the operating system can support standalone systems and was intended to be used as part of Valve's [[Steam Machines|Steam Machine]] platform. SteamOS versions 1.0, released in December 2013, and 2.0 were based on the [[Debian]] distribution of Linux with [[GNOME]] desktop.<ref>{{cite web |last=Makuch |first=Eddie |date=September 25, 2013 |title=Valve reveals Steam Machines |url=http://uk.gamespot.com/news/valve-reveals-steam-machines-6414959 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130930035955/http://uk.gamespot.com/news/valve-reveals-steam-machines-6414959 |archive-date=September 30, 2013 |access-date=September 30, 2013 |work=[[GameSpot]] |df=mdy-all}}</ref> With SteamOS, Valve encouraged developers to incorporate Linux compatibility into their releases to better support Linux gaming options.

In February 2022, Valve released the [[Handheld PC|handheld]] [[gaming computer]] [[Steam Deck]] running SteamOS 3.0. SteamOS 3 is based on the [[Arch Linux]] distribution with [[KDE Plasma 5]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/steam-deck-is-an-amd-powered-handheld-pc-from-valve-that-runs-kde-on-arch-linux/|title=Steam Deck is an AMD-powered handheld PC from Valve that runs KDE on Arch Linux|last=Duckett|first=Chris|date=July 16, 2021|website=[[ZDNet]]|access-date=July 16, 2021}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Tech Specs|url=https://www.steamdeck.com/en/tech|access-date=July 16, 2021|website=Steam Deck|publisher=[[Valve Corporation]]}}</ref>

===Tizen===
{{Main|Tizen}}
Tizen (based on the Linux kernel) is a mobile operating system hosted by Linux Foundation, together with support from the Tizen Association, guided by a Technical Steering Group composed of Intel and Samsung.

Tizen is an operating system for devices including smartphones, tablets, [[in-car entertainment|In-Vehicle Infotainment]] (IVI) devices, however currently it mainly focuses on wearable and smart TVs. It is an open source system (however the SDK was closed-source and proprietary) that aims to offer a consistent user experience across devices. Tizen's main components are the Linux kernel and the [[WebKit]] runtime. According to Intel, Tizen "combines the best of LiMo and MeeGo." [[HTML5]] apps are emphasized, with MeeGo encouraging its members to transition to Tizen, stating that the "future belongs to HTML5-based applications, outside of a relatively small percentage of apps, and we are firmly convinced that our investment needs to shift toward HTML5." Tizen will be targeted at a variety of platforms such as handsets, touch pc, smart TVs and in-vehicle entertainment.<ref>[https://www.tizen.org/blogs/dawnfoster/2011/welcome-tizen Welcome to Tizen!] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111013071516/https://www.tizen.org/blogs/dawnfoster/2011/welcome-tizen |date=October 13, 2011}}. Tizen.org (September 27, 2011). Retrieved on July 3, 2012.</ref><ref>Ricker, Thomas. (September 28, 2011)[http://thisismynext.com/2011/09/28/meego-dead-meet-tizen-open-source-os-based-linux/ MeeGo is dead: Meet Tizen, another new open source OS based on Linux] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930051802/http://thisismynext.com/2011/09/28/meego-dead-meet-tizen-open-source-os-based-linux/ |date=September 30, 2011}}. Thisismynext.com. Retrieved on July 3, 2012.</ref> On May 17, 2013, Tizen released version 2.1, code-named Nectarine.<ref name="tizen2_1">{{cite web |url=https://www.tizen.org/blogs/tsg/2013/tizen-2.1-sdk-and-source-code-release |title=Tizen 2.1 SDK and Source Code Release |publisher=Tizen.org |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130730123852/https://www.tizen.org/blogs/tsg/2013/tizen-2.1-sdk-and-source-code-release |archive-date=July 30, 2013}}</ref>

While Tizen itself was open source, most of the UX and UI layer that was developed by Samsung was mainly closed-source and proprietary, such as the TouchWiz UI on the Samsung Z's series smartphone and One UI for their Galaxy Watch wearable lines.

Note that some refrigerators use Tizen,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Side-by-Side Refrigerator with Family Hub (RS27T5561SR) {{!}} Samsung US|url=https://www.samsung.com/us/home-appliances/refrigerators/side-by-side/26-7-cu-ft-large-capacity-side-by-side-refrigerator-with-touch-screen-family-hub--in-stainless-steel-rs27t5561sr-aa/|access-date=2020-06-25|website=Samsung Electronics America|language=en-US}}</ref> even though they are not considered mobile devices.

===KaiOS===
{{Format|date=March 2025}}{{Main|KaiOS}}
KaiOS is a operational system made by KaiOS Tecnologies based on [[Firefox OS|Firefox OS/Boot to Gecko]]. Unlike most mobile operating systems, which focus on smartphones, KaiOS was developed mainly for feature phones, giving these access to more advanced technologies usually found on smartphones, such as app stores and Wi-Fi/4G capabilities.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kaiostech.com/ |title=The emerging OS |website=KaiOS |language=en-US |access-date=March 27, 2019}}</ref>

It is a mix of closed-source and open-source components.<ref name="support.kaiostech.com">{{cite web |url=https://support.kaiostech.com/support/solutions/articles/35000078432-can-i-access-the-source-code- |title=Can I access the source code? • KaiOS |website=Support.kaiostech.com}}</ref><ref name="KaiOS/B2G repository">{{cite web |title=KaiOS/B2G repository |website=[[GitHub]] |date=January 10, 2022 |url=https://github.com/kaiostech/gecko-b2g}}</ref> FirefoxOS/B2G was released under the permissive [[Mozilla Public License|MPL 2.0]]. It does not redistribute itself under the same license, so KaiOS is now presumably proprietary (but still mostly [[open-source]], publishing its source code).<ref name="support.kaiostech.com"/><ref name="KaiOS/B2G repository"/> KaiOS is not entirely proprietary, as it uses the copyleft [[GPL]] Linux kernel also used in Android.<ref>{{cite web |title=KaiOS is doing well in India, but it's pulling some big numbers in US too |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/kaios-usa-india-958519/ |website=Android Authority |date=March 1, 2019}}</ref>

====Smart Feature OS====
[[HMD Global#Smart Feature OS|Smart Feature OS]] is a custom version of KaiOS that was developed and solely used by [[HMD Global]] for their KaiOS line of Nokia feature phone. The main differences between stock KaiOS and Smart Feature OS is the aesthetics such as icons, widgets, a custom Nokia ringtone and notification tone.

===Fully open-source, entirely permissive licenses===

====Fuchsia====
{{Main|Fuchsia (operating system)}}
Fuchsia is a capability-based, real-time operating system (RTOS) currently being developed by Google. It was first discovered as a mysterious code post on GitHub in August 2016, without any official announcement. In contrast to prior Google-developed operating systems such as ChromeOS and Android, which are based on Linux kernels, Fuchsia is based on a new microkernel called "Zircon", derived from "Little Kernel", a small operating system intended for embedded systems. This allows it to remove Linux and the copyleft [[GPL]] under which the Linux kernel is licensed; Fuchsia is licensed under the [[permissive licenses|permissive]] [[BSD licenses#3-clause|BSD 3-clause]], [[Apache 2.0]], and [[MIT license]]s. Upon inspection, media outlets noted that the code post on GitHub suggested Fuchsia's capability to run on universal devices, from embedded systems to smartphones, tablets and personal computers. In May 2017, Fuchsia was updated with a user interface, along with a developer writing that the project was not a for experimental, prompting media speculation about Google's intentions with the operating system, including the possibility of it replacing Android.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Amadeo |first1=Ron |title=Google's "Fuchsia" smartphone OS dumps Linux, has a wild new UI |url=https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2017/05/googles-fuchsia-smartphone-os-dumps-linux-has-a-wild-new-ui/ |work=Ars Technica |date=May 8, 2017 |language=en-us}}</ref>

====LiteOS====
{{Main|LiteOS}}
LiteOS is a discontinued lightweight open source real-time operating system which is part of Huawei's "1+2+1" Internet of Things solution, which is similar to Google Android Things and Samsung Tizen. It was released under the [[permissive license|permissive]] [[BSD licenses#3-clause license|BSD 3-clause license]]. LiteOS was used in the Huawei Watch GT series and their sub-brand Honor Magic Watch series.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

====OpenHarmony====
{{Main|OpenHarmony}}
[[OpenHarmony]] is an open-source version of HarmonyOS developed and donated by Huawei to the OpenAtom Foundation. It supports devices running a mini system with memory as small as 128 KB, or running a standard system with memory greater than 128 MB. The open source [[HarmonyOS]] is based on the Huawei [[LiteOS]] kernel and [[Linux kernel]] for standard systems. OpenHarmony LiteOS Cortex-A brings small-sized, low-power, and high-performance experience and builds a unified and open ecosystem for developers. In addition, it provides rich kernel mechanisms, more comprehensive Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX), and a unified driver framework, Hardware Driver Foundation (HDF), which offers unified access for device developers and friendly development experience for application developers.{{Citation needed|date=September 2019}}

Fedora Mobility is under developing mobile operating system by the Fedora Project that are porting Fedora to run on portable devices such as phones and tablets.
